 'We have to look at ourselves' published at 16:53 GMT 16:53 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth 
 Manchester United 
 Manchester United captain Harry Maguire, speaking to BBC MOTD: "Very disappointed. Coming to the game we wanted to get a win for our fans and to concede another set play for the first goal is not good enough.
 "We have to remain focused and when things aren't going your way you can't be giving away set plays. The second goal is a mistake and then we're 2-0 down at half time and we couldn't react.
 "There's a lack of confidence at the moment - the results, the performances we have to look at ourselves and find something within ourselves to bring more to the team.
 "That's every player that I'm talking about. When things aren't going your way you have to do the basics well and conceding set plays, a simple set play is just nowhere near good enough.
 "It's an individual thing - we have to stick together as a team. So early on in the season - we can still have a good season but something has got to change quick. It's been disappointing, that has to change."
 On backing manager: "We're fully behind Michael [Carrick], coming into the team last season he turned things around and got Champions League football this season. As individuals, we're not playing well enough."
 On downturn from last season: "When you play for this club you know you're two or three games away from that happening. You have to find something within yourself to help the club, help the team and get out of this. We will start winning football matches but we have to do it quickly."

 'It's not about me' published at 16:47 GMT 16:47 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth 
 Manchester United 
 More from Manchester United boss Michael Carrick speaking to BBC MOTD on fan reaction: "Mixed feelings - to feel the connection and appreciation from the supporters, I feel it and appreciate it a lot.
 "Mixed emotions - the situation we're in as a football club is what I care about the most. It's not about me. It's about this whole place and being in a better situation and position than we are at the moment.
 "It saddens me to have that feeling standing there. I feel so connected to it and there's an awful lot of responsibility and that's how I feel and I accept my role in it as well. To feel that from the supporters was special in a way - it's nice to have their connection and appreciation."
 Was it a farewell lap? "No not from me. There wasn't a tear, just appreciation for the fans and what they've showed me."
 Expecting conversations about future? "See what happens. I'm not expecting anything. It's just digesting today - we knew it was an important day to try and get us moving forward and we haven't done that. For me it's just digesting that and the emotions at the end of the game is something I've not really had before.
 "I've got the energy for sure - it means so much to me. You have games to focus on and gathering the players. The responsibility of doing that I enjoy that - I love it, it's what I'm here for."

 'Mixed emotions standing on the touchline' published at 16:43 GMT 16:43 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth 
 Manchester United 
 Manchester United manager Michael Carrick, speaking to BBC MOTD: "A tough day - the boys went into the game with the best intentions They found it difficult today - bit of tension, anxiety and a bit unsure. It made it difficult.
 "The two goals before half-time put us in a challenging position. The next goal then is important and I could feel the fans wanting to get behind us even at half-time I could feel the noise and willingness to get us forward. I spoke about that at half-time.
 "If we got that at that point then the whole dynamic would be changed but we couldn't get that at the point. Third goal finished the game in many ways. Mixed emotions - you could feel the boys trying to do the right things but you could feel the emotion in the stadium too and it was very mixed feelings for me standing on that touchline.
 "The free-kick against Ayden [Heaven] when he only tackled the ball, there was no one he tackled but the referee gave the free-kick. The free-kick we need to defend better. Leny [Yoro] slipped, he's bitterly disappointed. He's learning and he's made one mistake today. That won't affect him, he's a top player. The wind takes the ball and it's a good finish from the third."
 On leaving Bruno Fernandes on the bench: "He's fit and available but we decided to pick the team that we did today. Unfortunately for everyone we didn't manage to get the right result."
 "We want to push forward and create more, we could've done certain things but not enough really and that's pretty clear."

 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Alexander Isak has scored in three consecutive Premier League appearances for the first time since January 2025 when he struck in eight in a row for Newcastle
 By Michael Emons BBC Sport journalist Liverpool recorded their first home Premier League win of the season thanks to an impressive performance against in-form Brighton. 
 Two goals in a five-minute first half spell - an own goal from Seagulls midfielder Pascal Gross followed by Alexander Isak's sixth goal of the season - put the Reds in control.
 They should have conceded before the goals came, but Brighton's Yasin Ayari fired wastefully over the top after a fine move from the visitors.
 Ayari's miss proved costly as Liverpool took a 17th-minute lead when Florian Wirtz's shot, which was going wide, was diverted into his own net by the unfortunate Gross.
 That was the first goal the Seagulls had conceded in the league since a 1-1 draw against Leeds on 5 September.
 Brighton's defence was breached again shortly after, when Bradley Barcola did superbly down the right wing to create a chance and his cross was met by Isak's cushioned volley to double the Reds' advantage.
 The visitors were nearly gifted a way back into the match when home goalkeeper Alisson lost possession when playing out for the back, but Ayari's shot rebounded off the foot of the right-hand post.
 Liverpool did enough to see out Andoni Iraola's first league win at Anfield as Reds boss - to follow two home Champions League victories and one in the Carabao Cup since he replaced the sacked Arne Slot in the summer.
 Brighton's loss was only their second in 13 matches in all competitions in 2026-27 and they stay third in the Premier League, with Liverpool moving up from fifth to fourth, one point behind the Seagulls.

 Published 1 hour ago 
 Have your say on Liverpool's display 
 What did you think of Brighton's performance? 
 Liverpool analysis: Iraola's side finding rhythm 
 Iraola's side are starting to find form, with this their fourth successive victory since a 3-0 loss to Manchester City in their previous Premier League match at Anfield.
 Since that defeat, the Reds have now scored 14 goals in four games, with big-name players showing their class in the Premier League and Champions League.
 Midfielder Wirtz has seen his performances come under huge scrutiny and debate since his move from Bayer Leverkusen in June 2025 in a deal that could rise to £116m.
 The German, impressive on this occasion before going off in the 65th minute, thought he had scored his first Premier League goal of the season.
 He was originally credited with Liverpool's opener, only for it to be later judged as a Gross own goal.
 Barcola and Isak, who also each cost more than £100m, linked up superbly for Liverpool's second goal with the Reds a constant threat on the counter-attack.
 Isak joined in a British record £125m move from Newcastle in September 2025, but he missed a large part of last season with a broken leg.
 But the Swede's total of six league goals this season is the second highest in the Premier League, behind only Manchester City's Erling Haaland on nine.
 Liverpool could and should have scored more.
 Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen twice saved to deny Cody Gakpo and also kept out an effort from Ronald Araujo. Ex-Seagulls midfielder Alexis Mac Allister headed wide against his former side and Isak fired another attempt over.
 At the other end of the pitch, the Reds' defensive performances have been questioned this season, but they produced a resilient effort in the second half to stop any potential Brighton fightback.
 Brighton analysis: Early miss costly for Seagulls 
 Brighton have made a superb start to the season, but this was not their day.
 They had a 5-0 win over rivals Crystal Palace last time out in the Premier League, while they have also progressed into the last 16 of the Carabao Cup and are unbeaten after two matches in the main phase of the Conference League.
 The Seagulls have never finished higher than sixth in English football's top division and their fans are hoping for a push for a Champions League spot after their impressive start.
 But after the win over Palace, boss Fabian Hurzeler was quick to shut down any talk that they could be involved in the Premier League title race, and how they cope with the extra fixtures will be a key factor.
 Games are coming thick and fast for Brighton, who drew 0-0 in the Czech Republic against Jablonec on Thursday in the Conference League.
 This was the second of five successive away matches and perhaps a reality check for Brighton's ambitions this season.
 Hurzeler was left to rue what might have been had Ayari put them ahead following a lovely move from his Brighton side, whose total of 23 goals is the highest in the top flight.
 Diego Gomez, a goalscorer from the halfway line against Palace, played a superb through ball to Gross and his pull-back found Ayari, but the Sweden midfielder could only shoot over when he should have scored.
 Brighton quickly found themselves two goals behind, and despite having more of the ball, securing 64% of possession, the visitors could only manage one shot on target as they failed to score in the Premier League for the first time this season.
 Both of these sides are next in action with Carabao Cup last-16 ties on Wednesday, with Liverpool at home to Chelsea. Brighton face another tough away task in the north west, at Manchester City.
